claims.text: Aging AlCoCrFeNi2.1 between 550°C and 750°C produces a ductile-brittle-ductile response, with peak brittleness near 600°C and recovered ductility near 750°C.
The as-cast alloy has a lamellar FCC/B2 dual-phase structure.
The FCC regions are enriched in Co, Cr, and Fe, whereas the B2 regions are enriched in Al and Ni.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy exhibits high room-temperature ductility.
The as-cast FCC phase is disordered and has low antiphase boundary energy.
The as-cast B2/FCC phase boundaries are smooth.
At approximately 600°C, near-stoichiometric Ni3Al-type L12 domains form within the FCC matrix.
L12 or short-range chemical ordering increases antiphase-boundary-related energy costs for dislocation motion.
High APBE at 600°C suppresses cross-slip and forces dislocations into planar slip bands.
Cross-slip-related dislocation configurations can create jogs that pin dislocations and require additional stress or thermal activation for unlocking.
B2/FCC interfaces become maximally jagged or serrated near 600°C.
Planar slip bands terminate at serrated phase boundaries, producing stress concentrations that initiate cracks.
At approximately 750°C, thermal energy reduces L12 chemical ordering and lowers APBE.
Aging near 750°C smooths B2/FCC phase boundaries, restores cross-slip, and blunts stress concentrations.
TEM will show peak L12 domain size or ordering and maximum boundary jaggedness at 600°C, followed by reductions in both at 750°C.
Suppressing chemical ordering by rapid quenching should eliminate the brittle window.
Artificial smoothing of the phase boundaries should eliminate the brittle window.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires both strong ordering and jagged boundaries for brittleness, but falsification condition (2) treats a low-order, jagged-boundary sample remaining ductile as falsifying. That result is instead consistent with the proposed coupled requirement because one required factor is absent.
